8720 /// A context in which code is being synthesized (where a source location
8721 /// alone is not sufficient to identify the context). This covers template
8722 /// instantiation and various forms of implicitly-generated functions.
8723 struct CodeSynthesisContext {
8724 /// The kind of template instantiation we are performing
8725 enum SynthesisKind {
8726 /// We are instantiating a template declaration. The entity is
8727 /// the declaration we're instantiating (e.g., a CXXRecordDecl).
8728 TemplateInstantiation,
8729
8730 /// We are instantiating a default argument for a template
8731 /// parameter. The Entity is the template parameter whose argument is
8732 /// being instantiated, the Template is the template, and the
8733 /// TemplateArgs/NumTemplateArguments provide the template arguments as
8734 /// specified.
8735 DefaultTemplateArgumentInstantiation,
8736
8737 /// We are instantiating a default argument for a function.
8738 /// The Entity is the ParmVarDecl, and TemplateArgs/NumTemplateArgs
8739 /// provides the template arguments as specified.
8740 DefaultFunctionArgumentInstantiation,
8741
8742 /// We are substituting explicit template arguments provided for
8743 /// a function template. The entity is a FunctionTemplateDecl.
8744 ExplicitTemplateArgumentSubstitution,
8745
8746 /// We are substituting template argument determined as part of
8747 /// template argument deduction for either a class template
8748 /// partial specialization or a function template. The
8749 /// Entity is either a {Class|Var}TemplatePartialSpecializationDecl or
8750 /// a TemplateDecl.
8751 DeducedTemplateArgumentSubstitution,
8752
8753 /// We are substituting prior template arguments into a new
8754 /// template parameter. The template parameter itself is either a
8755 /// NonTypeTemplateParmDecl or a TemplateTemplateParmDecl.
8756 PriorTemplateArgumentSubstitution,
8757
8758 /// We are checking the validity of a default template argument that
8759 /// has been used when naming a template-id.
8760 DefaultTemplateArgumentChecking,
8761
8762 /// We are computing the exception specification for a defaulted special
8763 /// member function.
8764 ExceptionSpecEvaluation,
8765
8766 /// We are instantiating the exception specification for a function
8767 /// template which was deferred until it was needed.
8768 ExceptionSpecInstantiation,
8769
8770 /// We are instantiating a requirement of a requires expression.
8771 RequirementInstantiation,
8772
8773 /// We are checking the satisfaction of a nested requirement of a requires
8774 /// expression.
8775 NestedRequirementConstraintsCheck,
8776
8777 /// We are declaring an implicit special member function.
8778 DeclaringSpecialMember,
8779
8780 /// We are declaring an implicit 'operator==' for a defaulted
8781 /// 'operator<=>'.
8782 DeclaringImplicitEqualityComparison,
8783
8784 /// We are defining a synthesized function (such as a defaulted special
8785 /// member).
8786 DefiningSynthesizedFunction,
8787
8788 // We are checking the constraints associated with a constrained entity or
8789 // the constraint expression of a concept. This includes the checks that
8790 // atomic constraints have the type 'bool' and that they can be constant
8791 // evaluated.
8792 ConstraintsCheck,
8793
8794 // We are substituting template arguments into a constraint expression.
8795 ConstraintSubstitution,
8796
8797 // We are normalizing a constraint expression.
8798 ConstraintNormalization,
8799
8800 // We are substituting into the parameter mapping of an atomic constraint
8801 // during normalization.
8802 ParameterMappingSubstitution,
8803
8804 /// We are rewriting a comparison operator in terms of an operator<=>.
8805 RewritingOperatorAsSpaceship,
8806
8807 /// We are initializing a structured binding.
8808 InitializingStructuredBinding,
8809
8810 /// We are marking a class as __dllexport.
8811 MarkingClassDllexported,
8812
8813 /// Added for Template instantiation observation.
8814 /// Memoization means we are _not_ instantiating a template because
8815 /// it is already instantiated (but we entered a context where we
8816 /// would have had to if it was not already instantiated).
8817 Memoization
8818 } Kind;
8819
8820 /// Was the enclosing context a non-instantiation SFINAE context?
8821 bool SavedInNonInstantiationSFINAEContext;
8822
8823 /// The point of instantiation or synthesis within the source code.
8824 SourceLocation PointOfInstantiation;
8825
8826 /// The entity that is being synthesized.
8827 Decl *Entity;
8828
8829 /// The template (or partial specialization) in which we are
8830 /// performing the instantiation, for substitutions of prior template
8831 /// arguments.
8832 NamedDecl *Template;
8833
8834 /// The list of template arguments we are substituting, if they
8835 /// are not part of the entity.
8836 const TemplateArgument *TemplateArgs;
8837
8838 // FIXME: Wrap this union around more members, or perhaps store the
8839 // kind-specific members in the RAII object owning the context.
8840 union {
8841 /// The number of template arguments in TemplateArgs.
8842 unsigned NumTemplateArgs;
8843
8844 /// The special member being declared or defined.
8845 CXXSpecialMember SpecialMember;
8846 };
8847
8848 ArrayRef<TemplateArgument> template_arguments() const {
8849 assert(Kind != DeclaringSpecialMember);
8850 return {TemplateArgs, NumTemplateArgs};
8851 }
8852
8853 /// The template deduction info object associated with the
8854 /// substitution or checking of explicit or deduced template arguments.
8855 sema::TemplateDeductionInfo *DeductionInfo;
8856
8857 /// The source range that covers the construct that cause
8858 /// the instantiation, e.g., the template-id that causes a class
8859 /// template instantiation.
8860 SourceRange InstantiationRange;
8861
8862 CodeSynthesisContext()
8863 : Kind(TemplateInstantiation),
8864 SavedInNonInstantiationSFINAEContext(false), Entity(nullptr),
8865 Template(nullptr), TemplateArgs(nullptr), NumTemplateArgs(0),
8866 DeductionInfo(nullptr) {}
8867
8868 /// Determines whether this template is an actual instantiation
8869 /// that should be counted toward the maximum instantiation depth.
8870 bool isInstantiationRecord() const;
8871 };
8872
8873 /// List of active code synthesis contexts.
8874 ///
8875 /// This vector is treated as a stack. As synthesis of one entity requires
8876 /// synthesis of another, additional contexts are pushed onto the stack.
8877 SmallVector<CodeSynthesisContext, 16> CodeSynthesisContexts;
8878
8879 /// Specializations whose definitions are currently being instantiated.

9195 /// RAII class used to determine whether SFINAE has
9196 /// trapped any errors that occur during template argument
9197 /// deduction.
9198 class SFINAETrap {
9199 Sema &SemaRef;
9200 unsigned PrevSFINAEErrors;
9201 bool PrevInNonInstantiationSFINAEContext;
9202 bool PrevAccessCheckingSFINAE;
9203 bool PrevLastDiagnosticIgnored;
9204
9205 public:
9206 explicit SFINAETrap(Sema &SemaRef, bool AccessCheckingSFINAE = false)
9207 : SemaRef(SemaRef), PrevSFINAEErrors(SemaRef.NumSFINAEErrors),
9208 PrevInNonInstantiationSFINAEContext(
9209 SemaRef.InNonInstantiationSFINAEContext),
9210 PrevAccessCheckingSFINAE(SemaRef.AccessCheckingSFINAE),
9211 PrevLastDiagnosticIgnored(
9212 SemaRef.getDiagnostics().isLastDiagnosticIgnored())
9213 {
9214 if (!SemaRef.isSFINAEContext())
9215 SemaRef.InNonInstantiationSFINAEContext = true;
9216 SemaRef.AccessCheckingSFINAE = AccessCheckingSFINAE;
9217 }
9218
9219 ~SFINAETrap() {
9220 SemaRef.NumSFINAEErrors = PrevSFINAEErrors;
9221 SemaRef.InNonInstantiationSFINAEContext
9222 = PrevInNonInstantiationSFINAEContext;
9223 SemaRef.AccessCheckingSFINAE = PrevAccessCheckingSFINAE;
9224 SemaRef.getDiagnostics().setLastDiagnosticIgnored(
9225 PrevLastDiagnosticIgnored);
9226 }
9227
9228 /// Determine whether any SFINAE errors have been trapped.
9229 bool hasErrorOccurred() const {
9230 return SemaRef.NumSFINAEErrors > PrevSFINAEErrors;
9231 }
9232 };

9277 /// An entity for which implicit template instantiation is required.
9278 ///
9279 /// The source location associated with the declaration is the first place in
9280 /// the source code where the declaration was "used". It is not necessarily
9281 /// the point of instantiation (which will be either before or after the
9282 /// namespace-scope declaration that triggered this implicit instantiation),
9283 /// However, it is the location that diagnostics should generally refer to,
9284 /// because users will need to know what code triggered the instantiation.
9285 typedef std::pair<ValueDecl *, SourceLocation> PendingImplicitInstantiation;
9286
9287 /// The queue of implicit template instantiations that are required
9288 /// but have not yet been performed.

9295 class GlobalEagerInstantiationScope {
9296 public:
9297 GlobalEagerInstantiationScope(Sema &S, bool Enabled)
9298 : S(S), Enabled(Enabled) {
9299 if (!Enabled) return;
9300
9301 SavedPendingInstantiations.swap(S.PendingInstantiations);
9302 SavedVTableUses.swap(S.VTableUses);
9303 }
9304
9305 void perform() {
9306 if (Enabled) {
9307 S.DefineUsedVTables();
9308 S.PerformPendingInstantiations();
9309 }
9310 }
9311
9312 ~GlobalEagerInstantiationScope() {
9313 if (!Enabled) return;
9314
9315 // Restore the set of pending vtables.
9316 assert(S.VTableUses.empty() &&
9317 "VTableUses should be empty before it is discarded.");
9318 S.VTableUses.swap(SavedVTableUses);
9319
9320 // Restore the set of pending implicit instantiations.
9321 if (S.TUKind != TU_Prefix || !S.LangOpts.PCHInstantiateTemplates) {
9322 assert(S.PendingInstantiations.empty() &&
9323 "PendingInstantiations should be empty before it is discarded.");
9324 S.PendingInstantiations.swap(SavedPendingInstantiations);
9325 } else {
9326 // Template instantiations in the PCH may be delayed until the TU.
9327 S.PendingInstantiations.swap(SavedPendingInstantiations);
9328 S.PendingInstantiations.insert(S.PendingInstantiations.end(),
9329 SavedPendingInstantiations.begin(),
9330 SavedPendingInstantiations.end());
9331 }
9332 }
9333
9334 private:
9335 Sema &S;
9336 SmallVector<VTableUse, 16> SavedVTableUses;
9337 std::deque<PendingImplicitInstantiation> SavedPendingInstantiations;
9338 bool Enabled;
9339 };
9340
9341 /// The queue of implicit template instantiations that are required
9342 /// and must be performed within the current local scope.
9343 ///
9344 /// This queue is only used for member functions of local classes in
9345 /// templates, which must be instantiated in the same scope as their
9346 /// enclosing function, so that they can reference function-local
9347 /// types, static variables, enumerators, etc.
9348 std::deque<PendingImplicitInstantiation> PendingLocalImplicitInstantiations;
9349
9350 class LocalEagerInstantiationScope {
9351 public:
9352 LocalEagerInstantiationScope(Sema &S) : S(S) {
9353 SavedPendingLocalImplicitInstantiations.swap(
9354 S.PendingLocalImplicitInstantiations);
9355 }
9356
9357 void perform() { S.PerformPendingInstantiations(/*LocalOnly=*/true); }
9358
9359 ~LocalEagerInstantiationScope() {
9360 assert(S.PendingLocalImplicitInstantiations.empty() &&
9361 "there shouldn't be any pending local implicit instantiations");
9362 SavedPendingLocalImplicitInstantiations.swap(
9363 S.PendingLocalImplicitInstantiations);
9364 }
9365
9366 private:
9367 Sema &S;
9368 std::deque<PendingImplicitInstantiation>
9369 SavedPendingLocalImplicitInstantiations;
9370 };

9372 /// A helper class for building up ExtParameterInfos.
9373 class ExtParameterInfoBuilder {
9374 SmallVector<FunctionProtoType::ExtParameterInfo, 16> Infos;
9375 bool HasInteresting = false;
9376
9377 public:
9378 /// Set the ExtParameterInfo for the parameter at the given index,
9379 ///
9380 void set(unsigned index, FunctionProtoType::ExtParameterInfo info) {
9381 assert(Infos.size() <= index);
9382 Infos.resize(index);
9383 Infos.push_back(info);
9384
9385 if (!HasInteresting)
9386 HasInteresting = (info != FunctionProtoType::ExtParameterInfo());
9387 }
9388
9389 /// Return a pointer (suitable for setting in an ExtProtoInfo) to the
9390 /// ExtParameterInfo array we've built up.
9391 const FunctionProtoType::ExtParameterInfo *
9392 getPointerOrNull(unsigned numParams) {
9393 if (!HasInteresting) return nullptr;
9394 Infos.resize(numParams);
9395 return Infos.data();
9396 }
9397 };

11487 /// The kind of conversion being performed.
11488 enum CheckedConversionKind {
11489 /// An implicit conversion.
11490 CCK_ImplicitConversion,
11491 /// A C-style cast.
11492 CCK_CStyleCast,
11493 /// A functional-style cast.
11494 CCK_FunctionalCast,
11495 /// A cast other than a C-style cast.
11496 CCK_OtherCast,
11497 /// A conversion for an operand of a builtin overloaded operator.
11498 CCK_ForBuiltinOverloadedOp
11499 };
11500
11501 static bool isCast(CheckedConversionKind CCK) {
11502 return CCK == CCK_CStyleCast || CCK == CCK_FunctionalCast ||
11503 CCK == CCK_OtherCast;
11504 }

11506 /// ImpCastExprToType - If Expr is not of type 'Type', insert an implicit
11507 /// cast. If there is already an implicit cast, merge into the existing one.
11508 /// If isLvalue, the result of the cast is an lvalue.
11509 ExprResult
11510 ImpCastExprToType(Expr *E, QualType Type, CastKind CK,
11511 ExprValueKind VK = VK_PRValue,
11512 const CXXCastPath *BasePath = nullptr,
11513 CheckedConversionKind CCK = CCK_ImplicitConversion);

11515 /// ScalarTypeToBooleanCastKind - Returns the cast kind corresponding
11516 /// to the conversion from scalar type ScalarTy to the Boolean type.
11517 static CastKind ScalarTypeToBooleanCastKind(QualType ScalarTy);
11518
11519 /// IgnoredValueConversions - Given that an expression's result is
11520 /// syntactically ignored, perform any conversions that are
11521 /// required.
11522 ExprResult IgnoredValueConversions(Expr *E);
11523
11524 // UsualUnaryConversions - promotes integers (C99 6.3.1.1p2) and converts
11525 // functions and arrays to their respective pointers (C99 6.3.2.1).
11526 ExprResult UsualUnaryConversions(Expr *E);
11527
11528 /// CallExprUnaryConversions - a special case of an unary conversion
11529 /// performed on a function designator of a call expression.
11530 ExprResult CallExprUnaryConversions(Expr *E);
11531
11532 // DefaultFunctionArrayConversion - converts functions and arrays
11533 // to their respective pointers (C99 6.3.2.1).
11534 ExprResult DefaultFunctionArrayConversion(Expr *E, bool Diagnose = true);
11535
11536 // DefaultFunctionArrayLvalueConversion - converts functions and
11537 // arrays to their respective pointers and performs the
11538 // lvalue-to-rvalue conversion.
11539 ExprResult DefaultFunctionArrayLvalueConversion(Expr *E,
11540 bool Diagnose = true);
11541
11542 // DefaultLvalueConversion - performs lvalue-to-rvalue conversion on
11543 // the operand. This function is a no-op if the operand has a function type
11544 // or an array type.
11545 ExprResult DefaultLvalueConversion(Expr *E);
11546
11547 // DefaultArgumentPromotion (C99 6.5.2.2p6). Used for function calls that
11548 // do not have a prototype. Integer promotions are performed on each
11549 // argument, and arguments that have type float are promoted to double.
11550 ExprResult DefaultArgumentPromotion(Expr *E);

11552 /// If \p E is a prvalue denoting an unmaterialized temporary, materialize
11553 /// it as an xvalue. In C++98, the result will still be a prvalue, because
11554 /// we don't have xvalues there.
11555 ExprResult TemporaryMaterializationConversion(Expr *E);

11632 // operands and then handles various conversions that are common to binary
11633 // operators (C99 6.3.1.8). If both operands aren't arithmetic, this
11634 // routine returns the first non-arithmetic type found. The client is
11635 // responsible for emitting appropriate error diagnostics.
11636 QualType UsualArithmeticConversions(ExprResult &LHS, ExprResult &RHS,

11639 /// AssignConvertType - All of the 'assignment' semantic checks return this
11640 /// enum to indicate whether the assignment was allowed. These checks are
11641 /// done for simple assignments, as well as initialization, return from
11642 /// function, argument passing, etc. The query is phrased in terms of a
11643 /// source and destination type.
11644 enum AssignConvertType {
11645 /// Compatible - the types are compatible according to the standard.
11646 Compatible,
11647
11648 /// PointerToInt - The assignment converts a pointer to an int, which we
11649 /// accept as an extension.
11650 PointerToInt,
11651
11652 /// IntToPointer - The assignment converts an int to a pointer, which we
11653 /// accept as an extension.
11654 IntToPointer,
11655
11656 /// FunctionVoidPointer - The assignment is between a function pointer and
11657 /// void*, which the standard doesn't allow, but we accept as an extension.
11658 FunctionVoidPointer,
11659
11660 /// IncompatiblePointer - The assignment is between two pointers types that
11661 /// are not compatible, but we accept them as an extension.
11662 IncompatiblePointer,
11663
11664 /// IncompatibleFunctionPointer - The assignment is between two function
11665 /// pointers types that are not compatible, but we accept them as an
11666 /// extension.
11667 IncompatibleFunctionPointer,
11668
11669 /// IncompatiblePointerSign - The assignment is between two pointers types
11670 /// which point to integers which have a different sign, but are otherwise
11671 /// identical. This is a subset of the above, but broken out because it's by
11672 /// far the most common case of incompatible pointers.
11673 IncompatiblePointerSign,
11674
11675 /// CompatiblePointerDiscardsQualifiers - The assignment discards
11676 /// c/v/r qualifiers, which we accept as an extension.
11677 CompatiblePointerDiscardsQualifiers,
11678
11679 /// IncompatiblePointerDiscardsQualifiers - The assignment
11680 /// discards qualifiers that we don't permit to be discarded,
11681 /// like address spaces.
11682 IncompatiblePointerDiscardsQualifiers,
11683
11684 /// IncompatibleNestedPointerAddressSpaceMismatch - The assignment
11685 /// changes address spaces in nested pointer types which is not allowed.
11686 /// For instance, converting __private int ** to __generic int ** is
11687 /// illegal even though __private could be converted to __generic.
11688 IncompatibleNestedPointerAddressSpaceMismatch,
11689
11690 /// IncompatibleNestedPointerQualifiers - The assignment is between two
11691 /// nested pointer types, and the qualifiers other than the first two
11692 /// levels differ e.g. char ** -> const char **, but we accept them as an
11693 /// extension.
11694 IncompatibleNestedPointerQualifiers,
11695
11696 /// IncompatibleVectors - The assignment is between two vector types that
11697 /// have the same size, which we accept as an extension.
11698 IncompatibleVectors,
11699
11700 /// IntToBlockPointer - The assignment converts an int to a block
11701 /// pointer. We disallow this.
11702 IntToBlockPointer,
11703
11704 /// IncompatibleBlockPointer - The assignment is between two block
11705 /// pointers types that are not compatible.
11706 IncompatibleBlockPointer,
11707
11708 /// IncompatibleObjCQualifiedId - The assignment is between a qualified
11709 /// id type and something else (that is incompatible with it). For example,
11710 /// "id <XXX>" = "Foo *", where "Foo *" doesn't implement the XXX protocol.
11711 IncompatibleObjCQualifiedId,
11712
11713 /// IncompatibleObjCWeakRef - Assigning a weak-unavailable object to an
11714 /// object with __weak qualifier.
11715 IncompatibleObjCWeakRef,
11716
11717 /// Incompatible - We reject this conversion outright, it is invalid to
11718 /// represent it in the AST.
11719 Incompatible
11720 };

11914 /// ReferenceCompareResult - Expresses the result of comparing two
11915 /// types (cv1 T1 and cv2 T2) to determine their compatibility for the
11916 /// purposes of initialization by reference (C++ [dcl.init.ref]p4).
11917 enum ReferenceCompareResult {
11918 /// Ref_Incompatible - The two types are incompatible, so direct
11919 /// reference binding is not possible.
11920 Ref_Incompatible = 0,
11921 /// Ref_Related - The two types are reference-related, which means
11922 /// that their unqualified forms (T1 and T2) are either the same
11923 /// or T1 is a base class of T2.
11924 Ref_Related,
11925 /// Ref_Compatible - The two types are reference-compatible.
11926 Ref_Compatible
11927 };

11937 Function = 0x4,

11939 ObjC = 0x10,
11940 ObjCLifetime = 0x20,
11941
11942 LLVM_MARK_AS_BITMASK_ENUM(/*LargestValue=*/ObjCLifetime)
11943 };
11944 };

12055 class ConditionResult {
12056 Decl *ConditionVar;
12057 FullExprArg Condition;
12058 bool Invalid;
12059 bool HasKnownValue;
12060 bool KnownValue;
12061
12062 friend class Sema;
12063 ConditionResult(Sema &S, Decl *ConditionVar, FullExprArg Condition,
12064 bool IsConstexpr)
12065 : ConditionVar(ConditionVar), Condition(Condition), Invalid(false),
12066 HasKnownValue(IsConstexpr && Condition.get() &&
12067 !Condition.get()->isValueDependent()),
12068 KnownValue(HasKnownValue &&
12069 !!Condition.get()->EvaluateKnownConstInt(S.Context)) {}
12070 explicit ConditionResult(bool Invalid)
12071 : ConditionVar(nullptr), Condition(nullptr), Invalid(Invalid),
12072 HasKnownValue(false), KnownValue(false) {}
12073
12074 public:
12075 ConditionResult() : ConditionResult(false) {}
12076 bool isInvalid() const { return Invalid; }
12077 std::pair<VarDecl *, Expr *> get() const {
12078 return std::make_pair(cast_or_null<VarDecl>(ConditionVar),
12079 Condition.get());
12080 }
12081 llvm::Optional<bool> getKnownValue() const {
12082 if (!HasKnownValue)
12083 return None;
12084 return KnownValue;
12085 }
12086 };
12087 static ConditionResult ConditionError() { return ConditionResult(true); }

12203public:
12204 /// Increments our count of the number of times we've seen a pragma forcing
12205 /// functions to be __host__ __device__. So long as this count is greater
12206 /// than zero, all functions encountered will be __host__ __device__.
12207 void PushForceCUDAHostDevice();

12209 /// Decrements our count of the number of times we've seen a pragma forcing
12210 /// functions to be __host__ __device__. Returns false if the count is 0
12211 /// before incrementing, so you can emit an error.
12212 bool PopForceCUDAHostDevice();

12214 /// Diagnostics that are emitted only if we discover that the given function
12215 /// must be codegen'ed. Because handling these correctly adds overhead to
12216 /// compilation, this is currently only enabled for CUDA compilations.
12217 llvm::DenseMap<CanonicalDeclPtr<FunctionDecl>,
12218 std::vector<PartialDiagnosticAt>>
12219 DeviceDeferredDiags;
12220
12221 /// A pair of a canonical FunctionDecl and a SourceLocation. When used as the
12222 /// key in a hashtable, both the FD and location are hashed.
12223 struct FunctionDeclAndLoc {
12224 CanonicalDeclPtr<FunctionDecl> FD;
12225 SourceLocation Loc;
12226 };
12227
12228 /// FunctionDecls and SourceLocations for which CheckCUDACall has emitted a
12229 /// (maybe deferred) "bad call" diagnostic. We use this to avoid emitting the
12230 /// same deferred diag twice.
12231 llvm::DenseSet<FunctionDeclAndLoc> LocsWithCUDACallDiags;
12232
12233 /// An inverse call graph, mapping known-emitted functions to one of their
12234 /// known-emitted callers (plus the location of the call).
12235 ///
12236 /// Functions that we can tell a priori must be emitted aren't added to this
12237 /// map.
12238 llvm::DenseMap</* Callee = */ CanonicalDeclPtr<FunctionDecl>,
12239 /* Caller = */ FunctionDeclAndLoc>
12240 DeviceKnownEmittedFns;
12241
12242 /// Creates a SemaDiagnosticBuilder that emits the diagnostic if the current
12243 /// context is "used as device code".
12244 ///
12245 /// - If CurContext is a __host__ function, does not emit any diagnostics
12246 /// unless \p EmitOnBothSides is true.
12247 /// - If CurContext is a __device__ or __global__ function, emits the
12248 /// diagnostics immediately.
12249 /// - If CurContext is a __host__ __device__ function and we are compiling for
12250 /// the device, creates a diagnostic which is emitted if and when we realize
12251 /// that the function will be codegen'ed.
12252 ///
12253 /// Example usage:
12254 ///
12255 /// // Variable-length arrays are not allowed in CUDA device code.
12256 /// if (CUDADiagIfDeviceCode(Loc, diag::err_cuda_vla) << CurrentCUDATarget())
12257 /// return ExprError();
12258 /// // Otherwise, continue parsing as normal.
12259 SemaDiagnosticBuilder CUDADiagIfDeviceCode(SourceLocation Loc,
12260 unsigned DiagID);
12261
12262 /// Creates a SemaDiagnosticBuilder that emits the diagnostic if the current
12263 /// context is "used as host code".
12264 ///
12265 /// Same as CUDADiagIfDeviceCode, with "host" and "device" switched.
12266 SemaDiagnosticBuilder CUDADiagIfHostCode(SourceLocation Loc, unsigned DiagID);
12267
12268 /// Creates a SemaDiagnosticBuilder that emits the diagnostic if the current
12269 /// context is "used as device code".
12270 ///
12271 /// - If CurContext is a `declare target` function or it is known that the
12272 /// function is emitted for the device, emits the diagnostics immediately.
12273 /// - If CurContext is a non-`declare target` function and we are compiling
12274 /// for the device, creates a diagnostic which is emitted if and when we
12275 /// realize that the function will be codegen'ed.
12276 ///
12277 /// Example usage:
12278 ///
12279 /// // Variable-length arrays are not allowed in NVPTX device code.
12280 /// if (diagIfOpenMPDeviceCode(Loc, diag::err_vla_unsupported))
12281 /// return ExprError();
12282 /// // Otherwise, continue parsing as normal.
12283 SemaDiagnosticBuilder
12284 diagIfOpenMPDeviceCode(SourceLocation Loc, unsigned DiagID, FunctionDecl *FD);
12285
12286 /// Creates a SemaDiagnosticBuilder that emits the diagnostic if the current
12287 /// context is "used as host code".
12288 ///
12289 /// - If CurContext is a `declare target` function or it is known that the
12290 /// function is emitted for the host, emits the diagnostics immediately.
12291 /// - If CurContext is a non-host function, just ignore it.
12292 ///
12293 /// Example usage:
12294 ///
12295 /// // Variable-length arrays are not allowed in NVPTX device code.
12296 /// if (diagIfOpenMPHostode(Loc, diag::err_vla_unsupported))
12297 /// return ExprError();
12298 /// // Otherwise, continue parsing as normal.
12299 SemaDiagnosticBuilder diagIfOpenMPHostCode(SourceLocation Loc,
12300 unsigned DiagID, FunctionDecl *FD);
12301

12347 // CUDA function call preference. Must be ordered numerically from
12348 // worst to best.
12349 enum CUDAFunctionPreference {
12350 CFP_Never, // Invalid caller/callee combination.
12351 CFP_WrongSide, // Calls from host-device to host or device
12352 // function that do not match current compilation
12353 // mode.
12354 CFP_HostDevice, // Any calls to host/device functions.
12355 CFP_SameSide, // Calls from host-device to host or device
12356 // function matching current compilation mode.
12357 CFP_Native, // host-to-host or device-to-device calls.
12358 };
12359
12360 /// Identifies relative preference of a given Caller/Callee
12361 /// combination, based on their host/device attributes.
12362 /// \param Caller function which needs address of \p Callee.
12363 /// nullptr in case of global context.
12364 /// \param Callee target function
12365 ///
12366 /// \returns preference value for particular Caller/Callee combination.
12367 CUDAFunctionPreference IdentifyCUDAPreference(const FunctionDecl *Caller,
12368 const FunctionDecl *Callee);
12369
12370 /// Determines whether Caller may invoke Callee, based on their CUDA
12371 /// host/device attributes. Returns false if the call is not allowed.
12372 ///
12373 /// Note: Will return true for CFP_WrongSide calls. These may appear in
12374 /// semantically correct CUDA programs, but only if they're never codegen'ed.
12375 bool IsAllowedCUDACall(const FunctionDecl *Caller,
12376 const FunctionDecl *Callee) {
12377 return IdentifyCUDAPreference(Caller, Callee) != CFP_Never;
12378 }

12390 /// Check whether we're allowed to call Callee from the current context.
12391 ///
12392 /// - If the call is never allowed in a semantically-correct program
12393 /// (CFP_Never), emits an error and returns false.
12394 ///
12395 /// - If the call is allowed in semantically-correct programs, but only if
12396 /// it's never codegen'ed (CFP_WrongSide), creates a deferred diagnostic to
12397 /// be emitted if and when the caller is codegen'ed, and returns true.
12398 ///
12399 /// Will only create deferred diagnostics for a given SourceLocation once,
12400 /// so you can safely call this multiple times without generating duplicate
12401 /// deferred errors.
12402 ///
12403 /// - Otherwise, returns true without emitting any diagnostics.
12404 bool CheckCUDACall(SourceLocation Loc, FunctionDecl *Callee);

12422 /// Given a implicit special member, infer its CUDA target from the
12423 /// calls it needs to make to underlying base/field special members.
12424 /// \param ClassDecl the class for which the member is being created.
12425 /// \param CSM the kind of special member.
12426 /// \param MemberDecl the special member itself.
12427 /// \param ConstRHS true if this is a copy operation with a const object on
12428 /// its RHS.
12429 /// \param Diagnose true if this call should emit diagnostics.
12430 /// \return true if there was an error inferring.
12431 /// The result of this call is implicit CUDA target attribute(s) attached to
12432 /// the member declaration.
12433 bool inferCUDATargetForImplicitSpecialMember(CXXRecordDecl *ClassDecl,
12434 CXXSpecialMember CSM,
12435 CXXMethodDecl *MemberDecl,
12436 bool ConstRHS,
12437 bool Diagnose);
12438
12439 /// \return true if \p CD can be considered empty according to CUDA
12440 /// (E.2.3.1 in CUDA 7.5 Programming guide).
12441 bool isEmptyCudaConstructor(SourceLocation Loc, CXXConstructorDecl *CD);
12442 bool isEmptyCudaDestructor(SourceLocation Loc, CXXDestructorDecl *CD);
12443
12444 // \brief Checks that initializers of \p Var satisfy CUDA restrictions. In
12445 // case of error emits appropriate diagnostic and invalidates \p Var.
12446 //
12447 // \details CUDA allows only empty constructors as initializers for global
12448 // variables (see E.2.3.1, CUDA 7.5). The same restriction also applies to all
12449 // __shared__ variables whether they are local or not (they all are implicitly
12450 // static in CUDA). One exception is that CUDA allows constant initializers
12451 // for __constant__ and __device__ variables.
12452 void checkAllowedCUDAInitializer(VarDecl *VD);
12453

12455 /// diagnostics and invalidates NewFD if not.
12456 void checkCUDATargetOverload(FunctionDecl *NewFD,
12457 const LookupResult &Previous);
12458 /// Copies target attributes from the template TD to the function FD.
12459 void inheritCUDATargetAttrs(FunctionDecl *FD, const FunctionTemplateDecl &TD);

12466 /// \name Code completion
12467 //@{
12468 /// Describes the context in which code completion occurs.
12469 enum ParserCompletionContext {
12470 /// Code completion occurs at top-level or namespace context.
12471 PCC_Namespace,
12472 /// Code completion occurs within a class, struct, or union.
12473 PCC_Class,
12474 /// Code completion occurs within an Objective-C interface, protocol,
12475 /// or category.
12476 PCC_ObjCInterface,
12477 /// Code completion occurs within an Objective-C implementation or
12478 /// category implementation
12479 PCC_ObjCImplementation,
12480 /// Code completion occurs within the list of instance variables
12481 /// in an Objective-C interface, protocol, category, or implementation.
12482 PCC_ObjCInstanceVariableList,
12483 /// Code completion occurs following one or more template
12484 /// headers.
12485 PCC_Template,
12486 /// Code completion occurs following one or more template
12487 /// headers within a class.
12488 PCC_MemberTemplate,
12489 /// Code completion occurs within an expression.
12490 PCC_Expression,
12491 /// Code completion occurs within a statement, which may
12492 /// also be an expression or a declaration.
12493 PCC_Statement,
12494 /// Code completion occurs at the beginning of the
12495 /// initialization statement (or expression) in a for loop.
12496 PCC_ForInit,
12497 /// Code completion occurs within the condition of an if,
12498 /// while, switch, or for statement.
12499 PCC_Condition,
12500 /// Code completion occurs within the body of a function on a
12501 /// recovery path, where we do not have a specific handle on our position
12502 /// in the grammar.
12503 PCC_RecoveryInFunction,
12504 /// Code completion occurs where only a type is permitted.
12505 PCC_Type,
12506 /// Code completion occurs in a parenthesized expression, which
12507 /// might also be a type cast.
12508 PCC_ParenthesizedExpression,
12509 /// Code completion occurs within a sequence of declaration
12510 /// specifiers within a function, method, or block.
12511 PCC_LocalDeclarationSpecifiers
12512 };

13030 // We check whether we're just after a comma in code-completion.

13125 /// Creates a SemaDiagnosticBuilder that emits the diagnostic if the current
13126 /// context is "used as device code".
13127 ///
13128 /// - If CurLexicalContext is a kernel function or it is known that the
13129 /// function will be emitted for the device, emits the diagnostics
13130 /// immediately.
13131 /// - If CurLexicalContext is a function and we are compiling
13132 /// for the device, but we don't know that this function will be codegen'ed
13133 /// for devive yet, creates a diagnostic which is emitted if and when we
13134 /// realize that the function will be codegen'ed.
13135 ///
13136 /// Example usage:
13137 ///
13138 /// Diagnose __float128 type usage only from SYCL device code if the current
13139 /// target doesn't support it
13140 /// if (!S.Context.getTargetInfo().hasFloat128Type() &&
13141 /// S.getLangOpts().SYCLIsDevice)
13142 /// SYCLDiagIfDeviceCode(Loc, diag::err_type_unsupported) << "__float128";
13143 SemaDiagnosticBuilder SYCLDiagIfDeviceCode(SourceLocation Loc,
13144 unsigned DiagID);
13145
13146 /// Check whether we're allowed to call Callee from the current context.
13147 ///
13148 /// - If the call is never allowed in a semantically-correct program
13149 /// emits an error and returns false.
13150 ///
13151 /// - If the call is allowed in semantically-correct programs, but only if
13152 /// it's never codegen'ed, creates a deferred diagnostic to be emitted if
13153 /// and when the caller is codegen'ed, and returns true.
13154 ///
13155 /// - Otherwise, returns true without emitting any diagnostics.
13156 ///
13157 /// Adds Callee to DeviceCallGraph if we don't know if its caller will be
13158 /// codegen'ed yet.
13159 bool checkSYCLDeviceFunction(SourceLocation Loc, FunctionDecl *Callee);
13160 void deepTypeCheckForSYCLDevice(SourceLocation UsedAt,
13161 llvm::DenseSet<QualType> Visited,
13162 ValueDecl *DeclToCheck);
13163};

13165/// RAII object that enters a new expression evaluation context.
13166class EnterExpressionEvaluationContext {
13167 Sema &Actions;
13168 bool Entered = true;
13169
13170public:
13171 EnterExpressionEvaluationContext(
13172 Sema &Actions, Sema::ExpressionEvaluationContext NewContext,
13173 Decl *LambdaContextDecl = nullptr,
13174 Sema::ExpressionEvaluationContextRecord::ExpressionKind ExprContext =
13175 Sema::ExpressionEvaluationContextRecord::EK_Other,
13176 bool ShouldEnter = true)
13177 : Actions(Actions), Entered(ShouldEnter) {
13178 if (Entered)
13179 Actions.PushExpressionEvaluationContext(NewContext, LambdaContextDecl,
13180 ExprContext);
13181 }
13182 EnterExpressionEvaluationContext(
13183 Sema &Actions, Sema::ExpressionEvaluationContext NewContext,
13184 Sema::ReuseLambdaContextDecl_t,
13185 Sema::ExpressionEvaluationContextRecord::ExpressionKind ExprContext =
13186 Sema::ExpressionEvaluationContextRecord::EK_Other)
13187 : Actions(Actions) {
13188 Actions.PushExpressionEvaluationContext(
13189 NewContext, Sema::ReuseLambdaContextDecl, ExprContext);
13190 }
13191
13192 enum InitListTag { InitList };
13193 EnterExpressionEvaluationContext(Sema &Actions, InitListTag,
13194 bool ShouldEnter = true)
13195 : Actions(Actions), Entered(false) {
13196 // In C++11 onwards, narrowing checks are performed on the contents of
13197 // braced-init-lists, even when they occur within unevaluated operands.
13198 // Therefore we still need to instantiate constexpr functions used in such
13199 // a context.
13200 if (ShouldEnter && Actions.isUnevaluatedContext() &&
13201 Actions.getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11) {
13202 Actions.PushExpressionEvaluationContext(
13203 Sema::ExpressionEvaluationContext::UnevaluatedList);
13204 Entered = true;
13205 }
13206 }
13207
13208 ~EnterExpressionEvaluationContext() {
13209 if (Entered)
13210 Actions.PopExpressionEvaluationContext();
13211 }
13212};

13235// Hash a FunctionDeclAndLoc by looking at both its FunctionDecl and its
13236// SourceLocation.
13237template <> struct DenseMapInfo<clang::Sema::FunctionDeclAndLoc> {
13238 using FunctionDeclAndLoc = clang::Sema::FunctionDeclAndLoc;
13239 using FDBaseInfo = DenseMapInfo<clang::CanonicalDeclPtr<clang::FunctionDecl>>;
13240
13241 static FunctionDeclAndLoc getEmptyKey() {
13242 return {FDBaseInfo::getEmptyKey(), clang::SourceLocation()};
13243 }
13244
13245 static FunctionDeclAndLoc getTombstoneKey() {
13246 return {FDBaseInfo::getTombstoneKey(), clang::SourceLocation()};
13247 }
13248
13249 static unsigned getHashValue(const FunctionDeclAndLoc &FDL) {
13250 return hash_combine(FDBaseInfo::getHashValue(FDL.FD),
13251 FDL.Loc.getHashValue());
13252 }
13253
13254 static bool isEqual(const FunctionDeclAndLoc &LHS,
13255 const FunctionDeclAndLoc &RHS) {
13256 return LHS.FD == RHS.FD && LHS.Loc == RHS.Loc;
13257 }
13258};

@ ThreeWay

@ None

@ Equal
This is an operator== that should be implemented as a series of subobject comparisons.
